 Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J.

1.  Heard Sri Gaurav Kakkar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajiv Dhar Dwivedi, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.1943 of 2016, Under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B of IPC and section 13(1)C / 13(2)/8 of Prevention of Corruption Act, Police Station-EOW (Economic Offences Wing) Vijaynagar,
District-Ghaziabad, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.

He next submits, as per allegation levelled against applicant, he was a guarantor against the loan disbursed in favor of co-accused Satya Deo Singh and as co-accused Satya Deo Singh by fraud obtained loan, therefore, applicant has also been made accused alongwith him.

He next submits, it appears co-accused Satyadev Singh was principal accused and he has been released on bail by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.25723 of 2025 vide order dated 14.08.2025, which is annexed at page no.65 of the supplementary affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.25723 of 2025
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 4. He further submits, FIR was lodged in the present case in the year 2017 and however applicant is fully cooperating with the investigation, but Investigating Officer suddenly arrested him on 25.9.2025, i.e. after almost eight years.

He next submits that even with regard to the applicant,
investigation of the case is still pending.
5.

He further submitted that apart from the present case, applicant is also having criminal history of one another case but in that case also applicant has been made accused with similar allegation and in this case he has been released on anticipatory bail even by the court concerned.

He next submits,
applicant is in jail in the present matter since 25.09.2025.
6. Per contra, learned AGA however, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. However, as per allegation, applicant was one of the guarantors of co-accused Satya Deo Singh,
who obtained huge loan of Rs.55,00,000/- allegedly on the basis of fake documents, but it reflects co-accused Satya Deo Singh, who appears to be the principal accused, has already been released on bail by this Court vide order dated 14.08.2025 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.25723 of 2025.
9.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Further, it also appears, though FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2017 but applicant has been arrested in the month of September 2025 i.e. after eight years and there is no allegation that applicant was not cooperating with the investigation.

sentences.text: Further, apart from the present case, applicant is also having criminal history of one another case but in that case he has been made accused with similar allegation and in that case he has been enlarged on anticipatory bail even by the court concerned.
Further, applicant is in jail in the present matter since 25.09.2025.
11. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant-Abhishek Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
14. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

15. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
(Sameer Jain,J.) November 6, 2025 Anurag/-
